# Field — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a field whenever you render a labelled control — it is the thing that makes a text box a form control rather than a box. It owns the association a screen reader needs: the label names the control, the description and the error are announced with it, and the error announces itself when it appears. Reach for the individual parts when you are composing something the field does not cover, but keep the wiring — a label that is not associated with its input is a label sighted users benefit from and everyone else does not.

### Anatomy

| Part | Role |
| --- | --- |
| FieldRoot | The stack. Groups the parts and owns the association between them. |
| FieldLabel | Names the control. Becomes its accessible name. |
| FieldDescription | Help text. Wired to `aria-describedby` so it is read with the control. |
| FieldError | The error line. Announces itself when it appears. |
| FieldMessage | The generic message line in either tone, used by `Input` to render its own error. |

## Native

### Features

Reach for a field whenever a control needs a name and somewhere to explain itself. The whole point is the wiring: the label, the description and the error are passed through context, and the control reads them so its accessible name and its described-by text are correct without you connecting anything by hand. `error` takes precedence over `description` — when there is an error it is shown and the description is not, because two messages under one field is two messages too many. The composition is a namespace (`Root`, `Label`, `Description`, `Error`, `Control`) so the parts are discoverable, and `Root` is also exported standalone as `FieldRoot`.
